title: Reserve Dynamic-Array Capacity
subtitle: What does geometric vector growth cost when the final size is already known?

metrics.label: CPU cycles
metrics.explanation: Cycles attributed to mesh construction, including inlined vector growth work.

metrics.label: Instructions
metrics.explanation: Extra growth checks and element moves increase the work retired by the processor.

metrics.label: IPC
metrics.explanation: Instructions per cycle helps distinguish less work from better processor utilization.

metrics.label: Cache misses
metrics.explanation: Reallocating and copying growing buffers can touch more memory.

learning.change: The optimized version reserves the exact capacities of all three vectors before appending elements.
learning.hypothesis: Preallocation should remove allocator round trips and repeated copies without changing the final mesh.
learning.caution: reserve() helps only when a useful capacity estimate is available; excessive reservation can waste memory.
prompts: Why is push_back still amortized O(1) even though some appends copy the whole buffer?
Which evidence supports less allocation and copy churn?
Why is this a constant-factor optimization rather than an asymptotic improvement?
